description.value: The study investigated disruption of global, local, and inter-regional functional brain network organization in patients with probable bvFTD compared with healthy individuals using resting-state fMRI and graph theoretical analysis, including relationships between network properties and executive function.

value: We hypothesized that brain damage related to bvFTD disrupts global brain network connectivity, and that patients with bvFTD have altered key frontal hubs and frontoinsular-temporal connections, resulting in limited functional capacity to integrate information across brain regions.

value: Global topologic organization of the functional brain network in patients with bvFTD was significantly disrupted, as indicated by reduced mean network degree, clustering coefficient, and global efficiency and increased characteristic path length and assortativity relative to controls.
Patients with bvFTD showed a loss of efficiency in information exchange between both close and distant brain regions.
Abnormal topologic organization of functional networks correlated with poorer performance on executive tests.

value: Local functional network organization was altered in bvFTD, driven by different localization of hubs and a preferential decrease in connectivity of the anterior cingulate, frontoinsular, and temporal cortices and subcortical nuclei.
Compared to controls, patients with bvFTD retained major hubs in the medial parietal, temporal, and occipital lobes but did not show hubs in the frontal lobes.
Decreased nodal centrality was noted in the anterior cingulate cortex, orbitofrontal cortex, caudate nucleus, insula, and some parts of the temporal lobes.

spans.text: We showed that local functional network organization is also altered in bvFTD, and that this change was driven by different localization of hubs and a preferential decrease in connectivity of the ACC, frontoinsular, and temporal cortices and subcortical nuclei rather than a nonspecific decrease of connection strength.
